en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect cone shape and is one of the most active Philippine volcanoes.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its entire brain.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Taal Lake in Batangas is located inside a massive volcanic caldera and contains Volcano Island with its own crater lake.
Abaca, a species of banana plant native to the Philippines, produces strong fibers used globally to make tea bags and ropes.
The Philippine Sea, located east of the archipelago, contains the Philippine Trench, which reaches depths of over 10,000 meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, the national bird, hunts monkeys and flying lemurs in the forests of Mindanao.
Batanes, the northernmost province of the Philippines, features traditional stone houses with thick limestone walls designed to withstand strong typhoons.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago using hand tools.
